# Purpose

Award credit for a defensible cantilever idealization, complete free-body diagram, consistent units, correct reactions and internal resultants, accurate rectangular-section properties, correct stress and deflection calculations, and an engineering recommendation bounded by the stated assumptions.

# Scope of the Base Problem

The arm is modeled as a straight, prismatic Euler-Bernoulli cantilever with an equivalent solid rectangular section, a perfectly fixed wall end, a concentrated equivalent static load, small deformation, and homogeneous linear-elastic steel. The model neglects self-weight, the actual hollow construction, bracket and anchor flexibility, bolt and weld stresses, local stress concentrations, load eccentricity in the backboard/rim assembly, fatigue, vibration, impact dynamics, and code-specific basketball-equipment requirements.

# Supplemental Assessment Structure

- context interpretation and load path: 20%;
- student idealization and assumptions: 20%;
- reactions, internal resultants, and section properties: 20%;
- stress, factor of safety, and deflection calculations: 30%;
